questions.question: Name and describe the four layers of a tropical rainforest.
questions.expected_answer: The emergent layer is made of a few giant trees, sometimes fifty metres tall or more, standing above the rest in full sunlight. The canopy is a thick roof of leaves, branches and fruit about twenty-five to forty metres up, where most animals live. The understorey is dim, with young trees, shrubs and large-leaved plants. The forest floor is dark and damp, covered with fallen leaves and dead wood, with few plants but many fungi, insects and worms.

questions.question: Explain three ways in which rainforest plants are adapted to their environment.
questions.expected_answer: Many leaves have drip tips that let heavy rain run off quickly so they do not rot. Tall trees have buttress roots that spread out like walls to support them in the thin, shallow soil. Lianas climb up tree trunks to reach the light, and epiphytes grow on high branches and take water from the damp air and rain. Most trees are also evergreen because there is no cold or dry season.

questions.question: What is biodiversity, and give examples of rainforest animals from different continents.
questions.expected_answer: Biodiversity is the huge variety of kinds of plants and animals in a place. Rainforests have more biodiversity than any other natural region on land, possibly around half of all the world's kinds. The Amazon has jaguars, sloths, toucans and poison dart frogs; the Congo Basin has gorillas, chimpanzees, bonobos and okapi; Southeast Asia has orangutans on Borneo and Sumatra, tigers and hornbills.
